interpretation.false_positive_floor: 17.1% of windows from papers written before ChatGPT existed score above 0.5, and 4.5% above 0.9. That is the detector's false-positive rate on definitively human academic prose at this window size, and it is why no single window can support a conclusion.
interpretation.window_size_finding: Window size was swept at 160/300/450/600 words. The human false-positive rate stays 16-21% at every size, so longer windows do not buy calibration -- but the Darwin public-domain control degrades badly with length (0.019 at 160 words, 0.79 at 450+). 160 words is therefore kept: best control behaviour, and the finest resolution for the curve.
interpretation.strata_gap: Published 2023-26 papers sit far above pre-2022 papers: median window 0.277 vs 0.079, share over 0.5 of 37.9% vs 17.1%. Consistent with widespread LLM assistance in current academic writing, but confounded with sample differences (venue-stated CHI-family 2023-26 vs general cs.HC 2018-21), so read it as a large signal of unknown composition, not as a measured rate of AI use.
interpretation.why_distributional: Both strata have p99 near 1.0, so 'windows above the human p99' is a vacuous gate. The manuscript is compared distributionally instead: its median window and its share above 0.5, against both strata.

_note: Per-window score arrays are omitted: they are derived from copyrighted papers. Percentiles, means and share-over-threshold are measurements and are published in full. Rebuild the full arrays with scripts/calibrate.py.
